title: Durable writer record and a guard inside every mutation
outcome: Durable writer record and a guard inside every mutation
acceptance: The store holds one durable writer record (mode, lineage, state, epoch, expected instance id, head id, validation with its count) and a `local` project's record says `local`; the changeset teaches `migration import` to add it to a store exported by the previous build, reports the conversion by name with its count, and a test imports such an export

Every transaction that changes the store reads the record first and refuses unless the project is `local`, or the state is `active`, the home holds the registration for the expected instance and the validation is usable; a test opens a connection, sets the state to `releasing` through a second connection, and shows the first connection's next write refused with `portable_released`

One test per write path shows the refusal on a frozen store: a work mutation, a note, a project memory, a `memories` listing that records a context generation, task memory, a control operation, an advancing `next`, a graph save audit, policy administration, projection repair, and import or restore into the store; the same test shows `show`, `ls`, a `memories` read, `next --peek`, `doctor` and a `store` backup push succeed

The private registration is durable outside all database paths being replaced and excluded from every store/portable backup. Prepared registration alone grants no authority; activation requires matching durable writer record and current remote ownership. Tests copy a store to another home, lose registration after publication and copy a staged/archived file: all remain frozen, and retry never mints a replacement instance. Full-store backup restore preserves the stored writer record in active/released/transitional states; it never resets to local or mints registration. Tests restore active/released copies in replacement homes and a pre-release copy on its original home after handoff: missing registration or stale fresh-remote validation refuses mutation, read-only inspection works, and missing private journals cannot be reconstructed through restore.
A test shows a `local` project's fourteen words and host control operations give the same results before and after the change, with no target configured

All ordinary opens, including raw, immutable, backup, diagnostic and migration helpers, obtain a shared lifetime guard before checking incomplete install journals and retain it through connection close. Installer exclusive acquisition refuses with live handles, takes locks in lifecycle-then-install order and performs no lock upgrade. Path alias tests and Windows separate-process tests prove reopening cannot race archive/install; old noncooperating binaries are an explicit cutover prerequisite.
disposal_reason: Portable handoff was replaced before any of it shipped: docs/features/git-task-sync.md says the previous portable writer-epoch and release/acquire design is gone, AGENTS.md says the selected sync uses no global writer lock, writer epochs or release/acquire protocol, and master has no portable code or brief. Cancelled under Greg's word, 43498a6e #683. Nothing here was built or tested.
